### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **76** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a105ad041a9da332bd38f6f5cafa86da7bba57ad` — the merge of head `2c055c088f2e75046eed9e17b8fa9203a38e3019` into base `c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a105ad041a9da332bd38f6f5cafa86da7bba57ad && git checkout a105ad041a9da332bd38f6f5cafa86da7bba57ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895 2c055c088f2e75046eed9e17b8fa9203a38e3019 && git checkout -B drift-repro c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895 && git merge --no-ff 2c055c088f2e75046eed9e17b8fa9203a38e3019

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c5b43b606807e26d873e2407cbd38a844e624895` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2b882e6774dda4bd54b14104da070b900fb6e5b2`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22877 (body and all 20 comments; ruling 6116165299, seat answers 6118224899, landing record 6121513183, stage-2 claim 6123966682, dev report 6127796890), PR #23070 (body, 14-file list, the net diff `df7a137923..2b882e6774`, fetched into `refs/review/pr-23070`), and the head's check-runs (REST, polled at 15:57Z, 16:06Z and 16:07Z). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head at 16:07Z: 40 runs; 29 `success`; 5 `skipped` (Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard, Packed-tarball smoke); 6 still `in_progress` — Test Core 1/6 through 6/6.** Every lint, type-check, changeset, docs, size, claim and single-writer gate is green; the suite verdict is not yet in. The verdict below does not rest on the running shards; a red shard re-judges this head.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, against the ruling's letter (A, Q2 i):

1. **The selector's name, `member` — right.** The discriminator's FIELD is `locale` (`ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS.email_template = { field: 'locale', canonical: 'en-US' }`), so a literal "named after the discriminator" would yield the one name the ruling forbids; the operative clause is "so it cannot be read as the UI translation locale", and the discriminator's stored name since stage 1 is `sys_metadata.bundle_member`. `member` is that name, type-neutral, and collides with no other query parameter on the REST surface (`'member'` occurs once in `rest-server.ts`, as `META_ITEM_MEMBER_PARAM`). Pinned at three points (`BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR`, `META_ITEM_MEMBER_PARAM`, the rest test's first case).

2. **The five closed query sets — right, re-measured from the head's handlers and the helpers they call.** GET `/meta/:type/:name` (handler from line 6369): the recognition gate is the handler's FIRST `req.query` read (6381); then `layers` via `wantsMetaItemLayers` (6480, reads `query.layers` only), `state` (6523), `preview` (6531), `package` (6542, 6845, and `serveMetaItemLayered` 4077), `locale` a frame down (`extractLocale` 6656 and `metaItemAnswerSources`, both through `metaRequestLocale`, which reads `query.locale` and nothing else). The whole-request helpers (`resolveExecCtx`, `resolveObjectMasker`, `anonymousFormIntakeWarnings`) read no query key, so no working read is turned into a loud 400. DELETE: `state` 7343, `dropStorage` 7352. `/history`: `sinceSeq` 7467 and `limit` 7476 through `readDeclaredQueryNumber`. `/publish`: `package` 7826. `/rollback`: `toVersion` 7968 (after the body's `toVersion`/`version`). Each handler opens with `refuseUnknownQueryParams` over an exported `readonly string[]` and adds `member` to its `refuseRepeatedQueryParams` list. Both pin halves exist per route in `rest-server-meta-member-selector.test.ts`: refusal (status, NESTED `error.code`, the exact `unknownQueryParamMessage`, protocol never called; plus the repeated-selector refusal) and preservation (the exact request object each protocol method received, `locale` and `package` included; GET's cache bypass with a member and its CONTROL without). In-repo callers (`client`, objectui at the pinned sha) send nothing outside the sets, as the dev measured; I did not re-measure objectui.

3. **The located 400 cases — right.** One reading, `resolveBundleMemberSelector`, refuses with `code VALIDATION_ERROR`, `status 400`, `param 'member'` and a sentence naming the selector: (a) a selector on a type with no discriminator, after the type fold (either spelling); (b) a non-string value (an adapter's nested parse, passed through by `metaMemberSelector`, never dropped); (c) a blank value, never read as absent; (d) a value over 100 characters, pinned equal to `SysMetadataObject.fields.bundle_member.maxLength`. The spec's `EmailTemplateDefinition.locale` is `z.string()` with no grammar beyond its description (BCP-47 by prose only), so there is no further "wrong value" the ruling's letter could ask for: a non-blank value of at most 100 characters can be a stored member, and one nothing holds is correctly the door's absent answer rather than a 400. Envelope: the route's recognition refusal is nested (`error.code`), the protocol-raised value refusal is flat (`body.code`) through `handleRouteError` — the pre-existing split `check:route-envelope` ratchets; same code on both. One note: the `?layers=` plus `?member=` refusal at 6489 is raised by the REST handler itself, not the protocol, and is also flat; it follows the handler's only pre-existing own-400 pattern, so it mints no new dialect, but the PR's deviation note ("the value refusal's envelope") does not describe it.

4. **The four spec request fields — right.** `GetMetaItemRequestSchema`, `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema`, `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema`, `HistoryMetaItemRequestSchema` each gain `member: z.string().optional()` with ONE shared describe (`BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION`), whose sentences match the implementation (absent means canonical, naming the canonical value is the same request, the four refusals, the absent-item answer). No `RollbackMetaItemRequest` exists in `packages/spec` (verified by search), and the REST door calls `rollbackMetaItem` through a cast (7871), so none was added — right. `authorable-surface/api.json` gains exactly the 4 keys; `protocol.mdx` gains the 4 rows. The spec gates are in the dev's 118 and CI's Lint jobs are green.

5. **The registry's bare-name canonical read — right.** `SchemaRegistry.getItem` on a discriminated type now answers `entriesOfMember(tiers, canonical)[0] ?? tiers[0]` over the unchanged tier order, and a named member narrows every tier; `getArtifactItem` narrows the same way. Pinned: a `zh-CN`-only overlay no longer answers a bare read (the half-false premise in 6118224899 is closed). One edge, stated for the record: a bundle that ships NO canonical member keeps the legacy first-member answer on a bare read, while `?member=en-US` answers nothing — so "naming the canonical value is the same request" (the describe and the changeset) is not exact for that bundle; the ruling's letter ("absent means the canonical member") favours answering nothing. Deliberate per the code comment, unpinned, not blocking.

6. **`removeRuntimeShadow` keeping its artifact test at name level — right, judged.** A member-level artifact test cannot work for a member the package does not ship: `mergeArtifactProtection` grafts the bundle's `_packageId`/`_provenance` onto that member's hydrated overlay, so `removeOverlayEntry` refuses it as code, and the shadow tier is the only one that can retire it (the dogfood found exactly this residue). With a member named, only that member's shadow goes; with none, the group sweep stays for `unregisterItem`. Pinned in `registry-i18n-bundle-key.test.ts` for a shipped member, an unshipped member, a no-package bundle and the no-member sweep, and in the harness against a versioned package. The root cause — an unshipped member's overlay wearing the artifact envelope, so `isCodeArtifactBody` misclassifies it — is left in place; see ③.

7. **The package-batch doors and the cluster event — right; and yes, `MetadataMutationEvent.member` is a public-surface addition.** `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` headers carry a non-canonical member; the protocol's `listDrafts` and `listCommits` strip it, so both declared responses are unchanged. `publishPackageDrafts` promotes, captures, plans (`CommitPlanItem.member`, `commitPlanKey`) and attributes a failure per member; `discardPackageDrafts` and `revertStoredPackage` discard per member; `revertCommit` reads, deletes, restores, re-binds, heals and re-plans per member. `MetadataMutationEvent` gains an optional `member`, stamped on save, publish, delete, rollback and revert, read by `applyRemoteMetadataMutation`. That interface is exported from the package index (line 127) and is the `event` of `ClusterMetadataMutationPayload`, which a peer ACCEPTS from the wire — an additive widening of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s published surface, as is the `member?` header on the exported `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts`. The package is graded `minor`, so the level covers both; the PR's `Widens:` sentence names neither (see ②). Mixed-version note: a replica on the previous release ignores `member` and re-reads the canonical row, which is the pre-PR behaviour until that replica's next boot — transient and self-healing, not a correctness hole on either side.

8. **A well-formed member nothing holds, per door — right.** GET: `item: undefined`, REST 404 (pinned in the harness with `fr-FR` and in the dogfood after the reset and reboot). Publish: `404 NO_DRAFT` (pinned as the bare CONTROL, the same path). Revert: `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND` (pinned for another member's version). DELETE `reset: false` and history `{ events: [] }` are stated and measured by the dev but not pinned in the harness; both follow the existing no-row paths (the probe-first delete, the empty lineage) and nothing in the diff changes those answers.

9. **The runtime dispatcher (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`) — a silent-drop hole, a follow-up, not this PR's to close.** The dispatcher's item read mounts `GET`, `HEAD` and `PUT` only (`METADATA_ITEM_METHODS`; the other verbs are 405), reads `state`, `preview`, `layers`, `package` and `locale`, has no closed set, and never passes `member`: a dispatcher-only host answers `GET …?member=zh-CN` with the canonical member, which is the plausible wrong answer the closed-set rule exists to prevent, now that the name has a defined meaning on the sibling transport. Not this PR's: the ruling cites AGENTS.md route rule 5, a `packages/rest` ingress rule converted per lane; the claim's surface excludes `packages/runtime`; the dispatcher had no closed set before this PR and the hole is read-only (no reset, publish, history or revert is mounted there). It must become a card, not an acceptance note — ③.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/rest` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` patch. `Clause-②: yes` on PR body line 2 and in the changeset body, no arm (allowed: at most one). `check:changeset-no-major` and `Check Changeset` are green; that gate asks only that ONE touched package carry `minor`, so it cannot see the finding below.

- `metadata-protocol`, `rest`, `spec` at `minor` — right: each publishes an additive widening (the four request fields; the five routes' accepted name; the protocol doors' `member`, the event field, the repository header).
- **`objectql` at `patch` — wrong.** `SchemaRegistry` is exported on the package index, and four of its public methods — `getItem`, `getArtifactItem`, `removeRuntimeShadow`, `removeOverlayEntry` — each gain an optional `member` argument. That is a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface (a new accepted value), which the maintainer's WHICH LEVEL rule (`pr-automation.yml` lines 754–767, ruled 2026-09-04 decision batch #35 on #15294, restated in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header) grades at least `minor`: "the commit type may raise a bump but never lower it below what the act requires; a `fix(` that widens is therefore `minor`". The changeset body itself describes the new capability under this package. Recorded for the seat: stage 1 graded `SysMetadataRepository`'s new `member` options `patch` under `Clause-②: no` and was accepted (6120204973); that reading is not binding here, and the rule's letter is. Remedy: one line.
- **The `Widens:` sentence** names the five doors' query parameter and the four request fields — right as far as it goes. It should also name `MetadataMutationEvent.member` (exported type; the cluster wire payload), the `member` header on `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts`, and the `member` argument on the four `SchemaRegistry` methods. A PR-body edit; `Check Changeset` re-reads the body on `edited`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (6127796890), each answered:
- File surface (+`protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts`, +two regenerated artifacts): accepted — the census must record the re-scoped site and the definition's new parameter, and AGENTS.md requires regenerated spec artifacts in the same push.
- `removeRuntimeShadow` at name level: accepted, judged in ① 6.
- Response contracts unchanged (`listDrafts`, `listCommits` strip `member`): consistent with the ruling, which widens the doors' accept set, not these responses; the Studio consequence is a follow-up (below).
- No `RollbackMetaItemRequestSchema`: verified, accepted; the rollback door's `member` is declared by its REST closed set and the implementation signature only.
- Suite heads (objectql full before the last commit; rest full pre-merge): the Test Core shards on this head are the record of that; they are still running.
- Attribution trailer: not a contract matter.
- PR body line 3 (`Widens:`): see ②.

Out-of-scope findings (dev), each answered or escalated:
- Runtime dispatcher does not read `?member=`: judged in ① 9. **Escalated — the seat files a card for the runtime lane** (transport parity for the by-name member selector on the dispatcher's item GET, with a closed set or at least `member` read and forwarded); the dev's "noted, not filed" is not an end state for a silent drop on a public transport.
- `GET /meta/_drafts` and `GET /packages/:id/commits` do not serve `member`; Studio's `DraftChangesPanel` would open the canonical body for a second language's draft: pre-existing shape, but now a user-visible ambiguity that stage 1 made reachable and this PR makes addressable everywhere but there. **Escalated — a card** (the two list responses, `DraftChangesPanel`/`ResourceEditPage`, and the client SDK's `meta.*` methods gaining the selector; the claim excluded the SDK deliberately, so it is owed).
- `/diff`, `/layers`, `/audit`, `/published`, `/references` stay canonical-only; `?layers=` with `?member=` is refused: right under the ruling's list. Added by this review: `PUT /meta/:type/:name` declares no closed set (its reads are `mode`, `force`, `package` through `metaSaveRequestOptions` and lines 7161/7170), so `PUT …?member=zh-CN` with an `en-US` body is silently dropped and writes `en-US`; the ruling keeps PUT body-addressed, so the fix is PUT's own closed set refusing `member` loudly — the same per-lane conversion. **Escalated — one card** for the remaining by-name doors' closed sets, `PUT` included.
- MetadataService keyed by name alone: pre-existing; `getMetaItem` and the heal now accept its answer only for the addressed member — right.
- The flat/nested envelope split: pre-existing ratchet; see ① 3 for the handler-raised layered refusal the note omits.

Added by this review:
- The envelope graft: an unshipped member's hydrated overlay wears `_packageId`/`_provenance` via `mergeArtifactProtection`, so `isCodeArtifactBody` reads it as code. This PR routes around it in `removeRuntimeShadow`; every other `isCodeArtifactBody` consumer that meets a bundle member inherits the misclassification. **Escalated — a card to measure it** (`removeOverlayEntry` alone, the disabled-package gate, the layered view's provenance fields).
- Docs: the drift bot (6127777257) names 32 hand-written pages touching changed anchors, with `authorable-surface/api.json` uncovered. No hand-written page enumerates these five routes' query parameters (`content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx` and `references/api/rest-server.mdx` checked), so no stale list ships; `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx` line 219 describes the by-name read and could name `?member=` — optional, not blocking.
- Check-runs: six Test Core shards were still running at 16:07Z; their conclusions are the suite verdict on this head and are to be read before any arming.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-12T16:12Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript. It made 58 tool calls: reads, `git fetch` into a review ref, scratch files inside this PR's scratch directory, and one record write. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat re-read the blocking finding itself: `SchemaRegistry` is exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, the PR adds an optional `member` argument to its public methods, and the WHICH LEVEL rule (`pr-automation.yml`, the maintainer's batch #35 on #15294) grades an additive widening of an exported surface at least `minor`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22877-member-selector`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

The one blocking finding is ② — `@objectstack/objectql` graded `patch` for an additive public-surface widening the maintainer's WHICH LEVEL rule grades `minor`. Fold into the same patch round: the `Widens:` sentence naming the event field, the repository header and the registry arguments. Every judgment in ① holds at this head and is a delta re-read at the next; the three escalated cards are the seat's to file, not the dev's to build here.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2c055c088f2e75046eed9e17b8fa9203a38e3019`
Local-runs: none

Delta record after the FAIL on `2b882e6774` (6128093700). Inputs: card #22877 (body and all 22 comments; ruling 6116165299, seat answers 6118224899, landing record 6121513183, stage-2 claim 6123966682, dev report 6127796890, seat note 6128113137, patch-round report 6128562834), PR #23070 (the body as edited at 16:44Z, the 14-file list, the net diff `df7a137923..2c055c088f` fetched into `refs/review/pr-23070-r1`, the delta `2b882e6774..2c055c088f`, the drift-bot comment 6127777257 and the prior record 6128093700), and the head's check-runs (REST, read at 16:46Z). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on the head at 16:46Z: 48 runs, 41 `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 running, 0 failed.** The skipped seven are the opt-in and matrix placeholders (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard) plus the `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` runs of the 16:44Z `edited` trigger. Test Core 1/6 through 6/6 and the Test Core aggregate are `success` (the suite verdict the prior record was waiting on). `Check Changeset` is `success` on both triggers: the push at 16:14Z and the body edit at 16:44Z. Every lint, type-check, build, docs, claim, size and single-writer gate is green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The delta changes no code.** `2c055c088f` is one commit whose sole parent is `2b882e6774`; `git diff --name-status` between the two heads lists `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md` alone (+11 / −1). The net diff against the unchanged merge-base `df7a137923`, with `.changeset` excluded, hashes identically on both heads (sha256 `d48e30a8a632…`), so every code hunk is byte-identical to the one the prior record read. 14 files, +1385 / −105. No rebase, no merge, no force-push.

2. **The prior record's ① 1 to 9 therefore hold on this head unchanged**, and were spot re-read in the head's tree rather than taken on trust: the four `SchemaRegistry` methods (`getItem`, `getArtifactItem`, `removeRuntimeShadow`, `removeOverlayEntry`, each with the optional trailing `member`, the non-discriminated branches untouched), the `SysMetadataRepository.listDrafts` header (`storedRowMemberHeader`), the four spec request fields with the one shared describe, `MetadataMutationEvent.member` (stamped through `mutationEventMember`, empty for the canonical member and for every type with no members), and the five door request literals on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (`rollbackMetaItem`'s included).

3. **Two of the prior record's non-blocking notes are now carried in the PR's own text.** The handler-raised `?layers=` plus `?member=` refusal that the deviation note omitted (prior ① 3) is now a bullet under "The value refusal's envelope". The no-canonical-bundle edge (prior ① 5) is now stated in the changeset's code-user section ("A bundle with no `en-US` member still answers its first member"); the administrator section's "naming `en-US` is the same request" remains inexact for that one bundle, as before; unpinned, deliberate per the code comment, not blocking.

4. **Prior ① 9 (the runtime dispatcher's silent drop of `?member=`) is unchanged** and remains the seat's card, not this PR's; see ③.

5. **The suite verdict is now in.** The six Test Core shards the prior record could not wait for are `success`, so the derived gate families the head's check-runs answer are all answered green.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/22877-member-selector.md` at the head: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/rest` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor. PR body line 1 `Fixes #22877`, line 2 `Clause-②: yes`, line 3 `Widens:`; the changeset body carries `Clause-②: yes` too, one arm, no `BREAKING` banner, no ADR-0087 disposition (none is owed: nothing is removed or narrowed on a published surface beyond the closed-set conversion AGENTS.md route rule 5 prescribes and the ruling cites).

- **The blocking finding is resolved.** `@objectstack/objectql` goes from `patch` to `minor`. `SchemaRegistry` is exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` (line 37), and four of its public methods gain an optional `member` argument: a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface, which the WHICH LEVEL rule (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` lines 754 to 767, the maintainer's batch #35 on #15294) grades at least `minor`. The level now matches the act.
- **Each other level re-checked against what the diff publishes, under the same rule:**
  - `metadata-protocol` minor, right: `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (index line 3) accepts `member` on its five by-name door methods; `MetadataMutationEvent` (index line 127, and the `event` of the exported `ClusterMetadataMutationPayload`) gains an optional field; `SysMetadataRepository` (index line 141) serves an optional `member` on each `listDrafts` entry. The module-level `BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR`, `BUNDLE_MEMBER_MAX_LENGTH` and `resolveBundleMemberSelector` are not re-exported from the index, and the package has a single `.` export, so they are not published surface.
